messages.subject: linetype = 2 in PDF from Word
parts:
Hi all,

I often copy ggplot2 plots into a word processor (e.g. MS Word), and then save the document as a PDF for final distribution. Is this considered bad practice?

The reason I ask is, when I do so, if I happen to have dashed lines in the plot (linetype = 2; see example below), something strange shows up in the PDF image (compare the RTF document with the PDF to see).

Here's the code and data. Note the diagonal lines show up in the PDF but not the RTF, and are not called for in the code. Rather, it appears to be some kind of weird result when linetype=2.

DF<-data.frame(x=rnorm(10),y=rnorm(10))
ggplot(DF,aes(x,y))+geom_point()+geom_vline(xintercept=.5,linetype=2)+geom_vline(xintercept=-.5)+geom_vline(xintercept=1,linetype=2)

Any ideas how this might be avoided?






Adam Loveland
